w10_P4_000096: A test-track laboratory publishes a figure that is 8 times a converted total, because 8 identical benches run the same programme. That converted total is the kilojoule form of a number that is 5 times the reading from a single run. The reading from a single run is what you get by adding a fixed instrument offset of 26 J to the energy a shuttle of 9000 grams carries because of its motion. The shuttle's position along the bench in metres is modelled by the fitted curve 4x^3 + 1x^2, where x is the time in seconds, and its speed is the rate at which that fitted position is changing at the instant x = 1 second. What figure, in kilojoules, does the laboratory publish?
w10_P4_000097: A packaging plant's monthly return is 6 times its weekly return, and the weekly return is 9 times a daily figure. The daily figure is found by adding a fixed gripper preload of 23 N to a shift total, and the shift total is 6 times the force needed for one push of the plant's transfer arm. Each push accelerates a carton of 14 kg along the rollers, and the carton's acceleration in metres per second squared is the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 7x + 6 = 0. The roller bed is 3 m long, which never enters the force calculation. What is the monthly return, in newtons?
w10_P4_000106: A foundry ledger ends with a number that is 3 times a corrected reading, because 3 identical lines run side by side. The corrected reading is what remains after a frame tare of 23 N is taken off an earlier value, and that earlier value is itself what remains after a sensor offset of 13 N is taken off the raw load-cell reading. The raw reading is the force needed to accelerate a mould of 88000 grams along the transfer rail. The mould's acceleration in metres per second squared is the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 4x + 3 = 0. The rail sits 4 m above the floor, a height the ledger records but never uses. What number, in newtons, ends the ledger?
w10_P4_000111: A certification sheet closes with a value obtained by subtracting a calibration credit of 23 kJ from a total that is 10 times a converted single-run figure. That converted figure is what you get by adding a standing allowance of 20 kJ to the kilojoule form of one run's recorded energy. In a run, a carriage of 34000 grams is launched, and its speed in metres per second is the total of the squares of the whole numbers from 1 to 5. The recorded energy is the energy the carriage carries because of its motion at that speed. What value, in kilojoules, closes the certification sheet?
w10_P4_000113: A hoist report ends with a number found by subtracting a contractual credit of 14 kN from a converted reading. That converted reading is the kilonewton form of the force needed to accelerate a test weight of 9 kg on the hoist's arm. The acceleration in metres per second squared is worked out in stages: start from the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 10x + 16 = 0, add a drive contribution of 15, then add a further gearbox contribution of 3. The hoist's cable is 12 m long, a length that plays no part in the calculation. What number, in kilonewtons, ends the report?
w10_P4_000117: A crate yard holds 359 crates in one shed and 73 in another, and the manager works out the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly with nothing left over. The acceleration his conveyor applies, in metres per second squared, is exactly 7 times that number, and it is applied to a pallet of 195000 grams. The controller records the force needed to drive the pallet and expresses it in kilonewtons. That converted figure is multiplied by 2 for the two conveyors in the yard, and then by 9 for the nine yards in the region. Each shed door is 3 m wide, a dimension the controller ignores. What is the regional figure, in kilonewtons?
w10_P4_000118: A demonstration rail launches a puck of 6000 grams, and the puck's launch speed in metres per second is the sum of the whole numbers from 1 to 11. The logger records the energy the puck carries because of its motion and subtracts a fixed friction allowance of 24 J from that record. The result is multiplied by 12, because 12 pucks are launched in a session, and then by 10, because 10 sessions make up the course. The final total is expressed in kilojoules for the report. The rail is 8 m long, which the logger never uses. What total, in kilojoules, appears in the report?
w10_P4_000194: A laboratory air-gun brings a slug of 19000 grams up to speed in 2 identical stages, and each stage adds 4 metres per second from the pressure pulse plus 2 metres per second from the spring. The bench software records the energy the slug carries because of its motion at the end of the second stage. Because the programme fires 11 shots, that record is multiplied by 11. The software then subtracts a barrel-friction allowance of 8 J, adds a standing calibration offset of 24 J, and finally subtracts a housekeeping allowance of 18 J. The gun's barrel is 1.5 m long, a figure recorded but not used. What number, in joules, does the software report?
w10_P4_000119: A workshop's final entry is 8 J more than a number that is 4 times an adjusted reading, since 4 identical rigs are used. The adjusted reading is what you get by adding a fixed sensor offset of 26 J to the energy a trolley of 51 kg carries because of its motion. That trolley's speed in metres per second is found by taking the number of distinct groups of 3 that can be chosen from the workshop's 8 test masses and subtracting 29 from it. The trolley runs on a bench with 8 mounting points. What number, in joules, is the final entry?
w10_P4_000128: A gantry report ends with a value in kilonewtons, converted from the force needed to move a carriage of 134 kg along its beam. The acceleration used for that force, in metres per second squared, comes from a short adjustment: an operator adds 1 to a base figure and then removes 1 again before entering it. The base figure is the rate at which the carriage's fitted position curve 3x^3 + 1x^2 is changing at the instant x = 1 second, with x the time in seconds and the position in metres. The beam spans 9 m, a length the report notes but does not use. What value, in kilonewtons, ends the report?
w10_P4_000129: A stores clerk has 199 bolts of one type and 34 of another, and he finds the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly with nothing left over. A test carriage of 34 kg is then launched at a speed, in metres per second, that is 10 times that number. The bench records the energy the carriage carries because of its motion and subtracts a rolling allowance of 7 J from the record. The remainder is expressed in kilojoules, and a fixed instrument allowance of 14 kJ is added to it. The bench top is 2 m long, which is never used in the calculation. What figure, in kilojoules, does the bench report?
w10_P4_000130: A haulage summary ends with a number that is 15 kN more than an earlier value, and that earlier value was itself 4 kN more than a converted total. The converted total is the kilonewton form of a figure that is 9 times the force on a single wagon, because 9 wagons are coupled together. Each wagon of 116000 grams is accelerated by the locomotive, and its acceleration in metres per second squared is the rate at which the fitted speed curve 5x^3 - 4x^2 is changing at the instant x = 2 seconds, with x the time in seconds. What number, in kilonewtons, ends the summary?
w10_P4_000134: A plant report ends with a figure obtained by taking 30 N off an annual total. That annual total is 7 times a monthly figure, the monthly figure is 4 times a weekly figure, and the weekly figure is 9 times the force needed for one stroke of the plant's ram. Each stroke drives a die of 34 kg, and the die's acceleration in metres per second squared is 4 times the sum of 4 and 12. The ram's guide is 2 m long, a dimension that has no part in the force calculation. What figure, in newtons, ends the report?
w10_P4_000141: A test house publishes a number that is 12 times a site total, since 12 sites run the same programme. Each site total is found by adding a standing allowance of 22 J to a figure that is 6 times a single-shot value. The single-shot value is what remains after a windage allowance of 22 J is subtracted from the energy that a projectile of 27000 grams carries because of its motion. The projectile's speed in metres per second is 2 times the sum of 3 and 19. What number, in joules, does the test house publish?
w10_P4_000145: A test bench accelerates a slide of 106000 grams, and the acceleration builds during the stroke: the rate at which the acceleration grows, in metres per second cubed, follows 1t^2 + 0t, with t the time in seconds, and it accumulates from zero between t = 0 seconds and t = 2 seconds. The controller computes the force needed to drive the slide at the acceleration reached at the end of that interval and expresses it in kilonewtons. That converted figure is multiplied by 10 because the bench runs 10 identical slides. A fixed frame tare of 1 kN is then subtracted, and a further contractual credit of 13 kN is subtracted after that. What number, in kilonewtons, does the controller report?
w10_P4_000148: A depot counts 191 pallets on one dock and 378 on another, and the supervisor works out the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly with nothing left over. The tug's acceleration, in metres per second squared, is 11 times that number, and it is applied to a load of 157000 grams. The control system records the force needed to move that load and expresses the reading in kilonewtons. A fixed rigging allowance of 6 kN is then added to the converted reading. What number, in kilonewtons, does the control system report?
w10_P4_000153: A quality report ends with a value that is 11 times an adjusted figure, because 11 identical cells contribute. The adjusted figure is what remains after a calibration credit of 1 kJ is taken from a total that is 5 times a converted single-shot reading. That converted reading is the kilojoule form of the energy carried by a hammer of 45000 grams because of its motion at impact. The hammer's impact speed in metres per second is the largest whole number that divides both 148 and 179 exactly, with nothing left over. What value, in kilojoules, ends the report?
w10_P4_000159: A teaching bench publishes a result in kilojoules, converted from a figure that is 11 times a single-release reading, since the class performs 11 releases. Each single-release reading is what you get by adding a standing allowance of 28 J to the energy a glider of 4 kg carries because of its motion just after release. The glider's release speed, in metres per second, is the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 6x + 5 = 0. The air track and its supply are set up at the front of the room. What result, in kilojoules, does the bench publish?
w10_P4_000162: A dockside crane accelerates a container module of 197 kg along its rails. The module's acceleration during the pull, in metres per second squared, is the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 7x + 10 = 0. The load cell records the force needed for the pull, and the software adds a fixed rigging preload of 18 N to that reading. It multiplies the sum by 3, because the crane makes 3 identical pulls in a cycle, and expresses the cycle total in kilonewtons. That converted total is then multiplied by 5 for the 5 cranes on the quay. What is the quay figure, in kilonewtons?
w10_P4_000167: A logger fits the curve 1x^3 - 3x^2 to a trace, where x is the elapsed time in seconds. At the instant x = 4 seconds, the rate at which the slope of that fitted curve is itself changing gives, in metres per second, the speed of a probe of 11 kg. The system records the energy the probe carries because of its motion and adds a fixed offset of 20 J to it. The sum is multiplied by 2, because 2 probes fly on each pass, and the result is expressed in kilojoules. A standing ground allowance of 17 kJ is then added. The launch mast is 6 m tall, which plays no part here. What is the final value, in kilojoules?
w10_P4_000169: A shunting yard accelerates a wagon of 181000 grams, and the rate at which its acceleration builds, in metres per second cubed, follows 1t^2 + 7t between t = 0 seconds and t = 2 seconds, starting from zero at t = 0. From the acceleration reached at the end of that interval the controller subtracts a slack allowance of 11 to get the value it uses. It then works out the force needed to accelerate the wagon at that value. Because a rake holds 10 wagons, the figure is multiplied by 10; because 8 rakes are shunted per shift, it is multiplied by 8; and because 10 shifts make up the cycle, it is multiplied by 10 once more. What figure, in newtons, does the controller report for the cycle?
w10_P4_000187: A press-shop total is 9 times a line figure, because 9 lines run in parallel. Each line figure is 11 times the force needed for one stroke of a press, since 11 strokes make a cycle. In one stroke a tool of 139 kg is accelerated, and the acceleration used is 3 times a base value in metres per second squared. That base value is what the rate curve 1t^2 + 4t accumulates between t = 0 seconds and t = 1 second, with t the time in seconds since the stroke begins. What is the press-shop total, in newtons?
w10_P4_000192: A workshop has 106 washers of one size and 271 of another, and the technician finds the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly with nothing left over. He multiplies that number by 4 for the four channels of his rig, then adds a drive contribution of 22, and the result is the launch speed in metres per second of a slug of 24000 grams. The bench records the energy the slug carries because of its motion at that speed. Because the test calls for 10 identical launches, the record is multiplied by 10, and the total is then expressed in kilojoules. What total, in kilojoules, does the bench report?
w10_P4_000195: A machine-shop ledger ends with a value found by taking 4 J off a doubled figure, the doubling being for the shop's two identical benches. That doubled figure comes from a bench value that is what remains after a friction allowance of 16 J is subtracted from a run total, and the run total is 7 times the energy of a single launch. In one launch a carrier of 39 kg leaves the rail, and its launch speed in metres per second is the largest whole number that divides both 12 and 145 exactly, with nothing left over. The energy of a launch is the energy the carrier carries because of its motion as it leaves the rail. What value, in joules, ends the ledger?
w10_P4_000199: A rolling mill drives a carriage of 143 kg along its bed, and the rate at which the carriage's acceleration builds, in metres per second cubed, follows 2t^2 + 1t. Between t = 1 second and t = 2 seconds the acceleration accumulates from zero at the start of that interval, and the value reached at the end is the acceleration the mill uses. The control system works out the force needed to drive the carriage at that acceleration and multiplies it by 8, because 8 carriages run together. It expresses the result in kilonewtons and then multiplies by 10 for the 10 mills in the plant. The mill bed is 12 m long, a dimension that plays no part. What figure, in kilonewtons, does the control system report?
